This notebook relies heavily on: 

1. [Analyzing RNA-seq data with DESeq2](https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html)

2. [RNA-Seq workflow: gene-level exploratory analysis and differential expression](https://f1000research.com/articles/4-1070/v2)

3. [Beginner’s guide to using the DESeq2 package](https://bioc.ism.ac.jp/packages/2.14/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/beginner.pdf)

4. [Count Regression](https://stats4nr.com/count-regression)


## Strategy:

1. Load S13, S14

2. Subset only:

```
c("junction_aa", "clone_id", "duplicate_count", "group")
```

3. Aggregate, summing duplicate counts

4. Load S19, S20, S21

5. Subset only:

```
c("junction_aa", "clone_id", "duplicate_count", "group")
```

6. Aggregate, summing duplicate counts

7. Ensure all junction_aa's in S13/S14 are in S19/S20/S21

8. Apply model

**To ensure all junction_aa's are accounted for:**

`setdiff(a$junction_aa, b$junction_aa)`

`setdiff(b$junction_aa, a$junction_aa)`


Note:

> As input, the DESeq2 package expects count data as obtained, e.g., from RNA-seq or another high-throughput sequencing experiment, in the form of a matrix of integer values. The value in the i-th row and the j-th column of the matrix tells how many reads can be assigned to gene i in sample j. Analogously, for other types of assays, the rows of the matrix might correspond e.g. to binding regions (with ChIP-Seq) or peptide sequences (with quantitative mass spectrometry). We will list method for obtaining count matrices in sections below.


```{r}
source("~/VHH/lib/utilities.R")

root_dir <- "~/VHH/data/Cluster-DBs/phylogenetic_dbs/translated_dbs/culled_databases/"
list.files(root_dir)[grepl("Cleaned", list.files(root_dir))]
```




"17_VecF3_R3_S17-Cleaned19Apr24.csv"         

        


## Load and Prep Data

```{r}
files <- list()

# Populate files

files[["S13"]]<- "13_VecF1_R2_S13-Cleaned19Apr24.csv"
files[["S14"]] <- "14_VecF1_R2_S14-Cleaned19Apr24.csv"

files[["S19"]] <- "19_VecF1_R3_S19-Cleaned19Apr24.csv"
files[["S20"]] <- "20_VecF2_R3_S20-Cleaned19Apr24.csv"
files[["S21"]] <- "21_VecF4_R3_S21-Cleaned19Apr24.csv" 

for (nm in names(files)){
  files[[nm]] <- read.csv(paste(root_dir, files[[nm]], sep = ''), header = T, stringsAsFactors = F)
}

results <- data.frame()
for (nm in names(files)){
  tmp <- files[[nm]]
  
  tmp$group <- rep(nm, each = nrow(tmp))
  
  tmp$dist_nearest <- NULL
  
  results <- rbind(results, tmp)
}

dat <- results

rm(files, results, tmp)
```

## Subset variables of interest

```{r}
tmp <- dat[,c("junction_aa", "clone_id", "duplicate_count", "group")]
tmp$clone_id <- paste(tmp$group, '-', tmp$clone_id, sep = '')
```









## Aggregate

```{r}
df <- aggregate(duplicate_count ~ junction_aa + clone_id + group, data = tmp, sum)
```


```{r}
df <- clonal_statistics(df)



df$median_CDR3 <- factor(df$median_CDR3)
df$clone_id <- factor(df$clone_id)
df$abundance <- as.integer(df$abundance)
df$group <- factor(substr(df$clone_id, 1, 3))
```

## Model

```{r}
library(DESeq2)

# Create a count matrix with appropriate row names
count_matrix <- as.matrix(df["abundance"])
rownames(count_matrix) <- df$median_CDR3

# Transpose the count matrix
count_matrix <- t(count_matrix)

# Create a DESeqDataSet object
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = count_matrix, # Transposed counts matrix
  colData = data.frame(group = df$group), # Experimental conditions
  design = ~ group # Design formula
)

# Check the DESeqDataSet object
dds
```


```{r}
# Estimate size factors
dds <- estimateSizeFactors(dds)

# Fit the negative binomial model
dds <- DESeq(dds)

# Perform differential expression analysis
res <- results(dds)

# Summarize the results
summary(res)
```


**Note:**

```
Error in estimateDispersionsFit(object, fitType = fitType, quiet = quiet) : 
  all gene-wise dispersion estimates are within 2 orders of magnitude
  from the minimum value, and so the standard curve fitting techniques will not work.
  One can instead use the gene-wise estimates as final estimates:
  dds <- estimateDispersionsGeneEst(dds)
  dispersions(dds) <- mcols(dds)$dispGeneEst
  ...then continue with testing using nbinomWaldTest or nbinomLRT
```

```{r}
#dds <- estimateDispersionsGeneEst(dds)
#dispersions(dds) <- mcols(dds)$dispGeneEst
```



Instead we try:

```{r}
# Estimate gene-wise dispersions
dds <- estimateDispersionsGeneEst(dds)

# Set dispersion estimates
dispersions(dds) <- mcols(dds)$dispGeneEst

# Continue with differential expression testing
res <- nbinomWaldTest(dds)

# Summarize the results
summary(res)
```



```{r}
# Filter significant results
#significant_results <- subset(res, padj < 0.05 & abs(log2FoldChange) > 1)

res$padj <- p.adjust(res$pvalue, method = "BH")

```


```{r}
# Volcano plot
plot(res$log2FoldChange, -log10(res$padj), pch=20, main="Volcano Plot", 
     xlab="Log2 Fold Change", ylab="-Log10 Adjusted P-value", 
     xlim=c(-5, 5), ylim=c(0, 10))
abline(h=-log10(0.05), col="red", lty=2)
abline(v=c(-1, 1), col="blue", lty=2)

```

## Load and Prep Data

```{r}
root_dir <- "~/VHH/data/Cluster-DBs/phylogenetic_dbs/"

files <- list()

# Populate files

files[["S13"]]<- "13_VecF1_R2_S13_min_threshold_clone-pass.csv"
files[["S14"]] <- "14_VecF1_R2_S14_min_threshold_clone-pass.csv"

files[["S17"]] <- "17_VecF3_R3_S17_min_threshold_clone-pass.csv"
files[["S18"]] <- "18_VecF3_R4_S18_min_threshold_clone-pass.csv"

files[["S20"]] <- "20_VecF2_R3_S20_min_threshold_clone-pass.csv"
files[["S22"]] <- "22_VecF4_R4_S22_min_threshold_clone-pass.csv"

for (nm in names(files)){
  files[[nm]] <- read.csv(paste(root_dir, files[[nm]], sep = ''), header = T, stringsAsFactors = F)
}

results <- data.frame()
for (nm in names(files)){
  tmp <- files[[nm]]
  
  tmp$perc_abundance <- tmp$duplicate_count/sum(tmp$duplicate_count)*100
  tmp$group <- rep(nm, each = nrow(tmp))
  
  tmp$dist_nearest <- NULL
  
  results <- rbind(results, tmp)
}

dat <- results

rm(files, results, tmp)
```


## Ensure Clone_id is appropriately tracked

```{r}
dat$clone_id <- paste(dat$group, '-', dat$clone_id, sep = '')
```


## Aggregate

```{r}
df <- aggregate(duplicate_count ~ junction_aa + clone_id + group, data = dat, sum)

df$junction_aa <- factor(df$junction_aa)
df$clone_id <- factor(df$clone_id)
df$group <- factor(df$group)
```

## Model

```{r}
library(DESeq2)

# Create a count matrix with appropriate row names
count_matrix <- as.matrix(df["duplicate_count"])
rownames(count_matrix) <- df$junction_aa

# Transpose the count matrix
count_matrix <- t(count_matrix)

# Create a DESeqDataSet object
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = count_matrix, # Transposed counts matrix
  colData = data.frame(group = df$group), # Experimental conditions
  design = ~ group # Design formula
)

# Check the DESeqDataSet object
dds
```


```{r}
# Estimate size factors
dds <- estimateSizeFactors(dds)

# Fit the negative binomial model
dds <- DESeq(dds)

# Perform differential expression analysis
res <- results(dds)

# Summarize the results
summary(res)
```


```{r}
# Define contrast
contrast <- c("group", "S20", "S13")  # Compare S20 vs. S13

# Perform differential expression analysis with contrast
res_contrast <- results(dds, contrast=contrast)

# Summarize the results
summary(res_contrast)

```





























## Prepare data (Aggregating by )

```{r}
dat$duplicate_count <- as.numeric(dat$duplicate_count)

df <- aggregate(duplicate_count ~ junction_aa + group, data = dat, sum)

aggregated_df <- data.frame()

for (i in 1:100){
  aggregated_df <- rbind(aggregated_df, dat[sample(1:nrow(dat), 100, replace = T), c("junction_aa", "duplicate_count", "group")])
}

aggregated_df$junction_aa <- factor(aggregated_df$junction_aa)
aggregated_df$group <- factor(aggregated_df$group)
aggregated_df$duplicate_count <- as.integer(aggregated_df$duplicate_count)
```

```{r}
library(DESeq2)

# Create a count matrix with appropriate row names
count_matrix <- as.matrix(aggregated_df["duplicate_count"])
rownames(count_matrix) <- aggregated_df$junction_aa

# Transpose the count matrix
count_matrix <- t(count_matrix)

# Create a DESeqDataSet object
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
  countData = count_matrix, # Transposed counts matrix
  colData = data.frame(group = aggregated_df$group), # Experimental conditions
  design = ~ group # Design formula
)

# Check the DESeqDataSet object
dds
```


```{r}
# Estimate size factors
dds <- estimateSizeFactors(dds)

# Fit the negative binomial model
dds <- DESeq(dds)

# Perform differential expression analysis
res <- results(dds)

# Summarize the results
summary(res)
```


```{r}
# Define contrast
contrast <- c("group", "S20", "S13")  # Compare S20 vs. S13

# Perform differential expression analysis with contrast
res_contrast <- results(dds, contrast=contrast)

# Summarize the results
summary(res_contrast)

```
